title: Model completeness: embeddings and existential formulas
summary: Characterize when embeddings between models preserve every formula, using existential witnesses and Robinson’s test.
abstract: An injection between infinite sets preserves every property that can be expressed using equality, and an order embedding between nonempty dense linear orders without endpoints preserves every first-order property of a finite tuple. Model completeness asks when all embeddings between models of a theory behave this way. Robinson’s test reduces this demand to a question about witnesses: an existential statement with parameters from a smaller model must already have witnesses there whenever it has witnesses in a larger model of the same theory. We prove the test using the preservation theorems and obtain existential and universal descriptions of every formula. A theory of one-point structures shows why this property differs from completeness of a theory.
